newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia will be frontrunner for NATO entry - PM.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia will be frontrunner for NATO entry - PM.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said on his return from a visit to the United States on Sunday that Slovenia would without doubt be included in the first round of candidates for full membership of NATO.
Drnovsek received confirmation Slovenia was among the first wave of candidates to join NATO when speaking to the United Nations General Assembly, he told Slovenian news agency STA.

"The Prime Minister believes that Russian objections will not influence NATO's decision on the first group of new members, which apart from Slovenia will most probably comprise Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary," STA reported.

Drnovsek said a resolution on NATO expansion that had already been adopted by the U.S. senate listed Slovenia among the first four NATO candidates. Slovenia declared independence from former Yugoslavia in 1991.

He said Slovenia had only recently been admitted to the first group of candidates but had a good chance of entering the 16-member Western military pact because of its political and economic stability and its Western standards of democracy.
Russion objections to NATO expansion did not apply to Slovenia, which was never a member of the Warsaw Pact, the former communist military union, he noted.
"There are no special objections to our membership (of NATO)," Drnovsek said.
Slovenia, which faces its third multi-party general elections on November 10, hopes to join NATO as soon as possible as a means of ensuring greater political stability in the restless Balkan region.
